text: After a long journey, you finally arrive at your hotel, ready to relax. All you need is a stable internet connection to catch up or unwind.
But then you see the Wi-Fi options. Basic access for an outrageous fee, or a 'premium' tier that costs even more.
Your first thought? Pure hotel greed. They know you're stuck, so they're simply overcharging for something that's practically free elsewhere.
But it's not just raw cost. Hotels allocate limited bandwidth, charging for *guaranteed* service levels. Premium users get a dedicated slice, not a free-for-all.
This high price covers infrastructure, support, and the assurance of a reliable, fast connection when you truly need it, like for important work calls.
So next time you log in, you'll see the cost not as pure profit, but as a system managing demand and guaranteeing quality for those who pay for it.
